newsitem.title: FRANCE: SMH reaffirms it sees higher 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: SMH reaffirms it sees higher 1996 net.

text.p: Nicolas Hayek, chairman of Swiss watchmaker Suisse Microelectronique et d'Horlogerie (SMH), reiterated he expected the company's 1996 net profit to improve.
Asked if he thought the group's profit would rise this year, Hayek said "yes," but he gave no further details.

"SMH is doing very well," he told Reuters at a presentation of production facilities for the Smart Car that SMH is building with Daimler-Benz AG. "We have made a lot of gains and revenue and volume sales are rising."
If sales during the Christmas season are strong, SMH may raise its dividend, he said, but added this was a matter for the board of directors to decide.
Asked if the dividend would rise, he said: "If Christmas business is very positive, but I cannot say this or else I will get into trouble with the board," he said.
Hayek in August described as "serious" analysts' forecasts that SMH profit could rise 18 percent in 1996. SMH net profit fell 13 percent to 273 million Swiss francs in 1995.
